findings.summary: Subagent/runtime reaper goroutines leak on two NewContainer constructor error paths.
evidence: go vet flags both cancel funcs directly: stopReaper (line 1162) and stopRuntimeReaper (line 1182) not used on all paths.
Two confirmed early-return paths (container.go:1242, 1246) return (nil, err) after the reapers are already started but before the cancel funcs are captured into the struct at lines 1398/1400.
Caller never receives a *Container on these paths, so it has no way to stop the leaked reaper goroutines.
findings.recommendation: Ensure every error return between reaper start and struct assembly also calls stopReaper()/stopRuntimeReaper(), matching the existing stopCatalog() cleanup pattern already present at both flagged sites.
findings.false_positive_considerations: If NewContainer failures are effectively fatal (process exits immediately), the leak is real but inconsequential in practice.
findings.revalidation_note: Confirmed still open: container.go changed since the audit (additive SkillVendor/ReflexEngine wiring), but the bug is intact -- exactly 2 return-nil-err paths exist between reaper start (line 1213) and struct assembly (durableAgentRecipes err at :1291-1293, SyncManagedDurableAgentConfigs err at :1295-1297, shifted from the audit's 1242/1246), and neither calls stopReaper()/stopRuntimeReaper(). Matches the finding's recommended fix pattern (mirror stopCatalog()) exactly.

A2APushNotifier is the sole outbound URL consumer and now reuses the internal/ssrf policy consolidated by GO-SEC4-007/task 08/09: HTTPS-only default, all-answer validation, pinned-literal dialing, and redirect revalidation. findings.recommendation: Register a lightweight 'queued' cancellation hook before acquireSpawnSlot is attempted, or re-check the row's current status immediately after acquiring a slot before invoking the runner.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Data integrity is not at risk -- finalizeRun's reconciliation correctly prevents a stale/wrong terminal status; only the run itself proceeds when it shouldn't.
findings.revalidation_note: Confirmed still open: in Spawn (service.go:868-919), `run.Status = StatusRunning` and `svc.emitStatus(run, "")` (the running broadcast) both happen at :871/:879, before `acquireSpawnSlot` at :891/:909, and `svc.cancelers[run.ID]` is only registered after the slot is acquired (:895-897, :913-915) -- a run canceled while queued has no registered canceler yet.

findings.summary: worktree.gitManager.CleanupOrphaned computes the wrong (8-char-truncated) branch name and therefore never deletes the actual orphaned git branch Create made with the full ULID session ID -- runs on every daemon boot, so every cleanup leaves a permanent stray branch, accumulating unboundedly across restarts/crashes.
evidence: manager.go:86 (Create, full sessionID) vs :166-170 (CleanupOrphaned, truncated to 8 chars); existing regression test only asserts directory removal, never that the branch is gone.
findings.recommendation: CleanupOrphaned should reconstruct the branch name identically to Create (full sessionID, no truncation).
findings.revalidation_note: Confirmed still open and unchanged: manager.go:86 (Create) uses the full `sessionID` for the branch name, while CleanupOrphaned (manager.go:166-170) truncates to 8 chars before building `branch := "worker-" + short` -- the two never match, so the orphan branch is never actually deleted. No commits touched internal/worktree/ since the audit.
